leading_positions.synthesis: Five members prefer B039 as a single-part prize for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. All five stress the theory-to-experiment chain (Kane-Mele Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall proposal, then observation of edge transport in HgTe wells), about two decades of independent confirmation, and the argument that it complements rather than repeats the 2016 topological-phases prize. All five also name the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and of the 3D topological-insulator work, as the main weakness, and several say it cannot be repaired within the supplied names. All five favour a citation scoped to the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 invariant, not to topological insulators broadly. Three of the five (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig) ranked it first in the opening; Olsson and Pearce state that they moved to it after reading the other ballots. Kroll ranked it eighth and Danielsson fourth, so the support is not unanimous.

Two members prefer B022 alone as a two-person prize for Katori and Ye. They share the view that it has the cleanest allocation on the shortlist, is reproduced across independent laboratories at the 10^-18 level, and is distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes because it concerns many neutral atoms at a magic wavelength. They differ in emphasis: Kroll argues that the pending redefinition of the second is irrelevant to physics merit and discloses a research stay in Hall's laboratory, while Lindroth treats the pending redefinition as a caveat and stresses that other lattice-clock and ion-clock groups are not covered by the credit. Both name B039 as their first alternative or close second.

One member proposes a two-part prize pairing the lattice clock (Katori, Ye) with the IceCube neutrino discovery (Halzen alone), for three laureates in total. He ranks B003 first in the opening, but his own case_against names the single-name credit for a collaboration-scale discovery as the weakest part of the configuration, and he says he would rather B022 or B039 stood alone if the committee judges that attribution too thin. No other member lists B003 in their configuration, and several (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson) say they would not support it with the present one-name credit. The chair, who also ranked B003 first in the opening, keeps it only as a second alternative.

areas_of_agreement: B039 and B022 are both regarded as scientifically strong, mature and independently confirmed; the disagreement is about ranking, credit and timing, not about whether the underlying results are real.

No member contests the existence of the IceCube diffuse flux; the objection to B003 is attribution (one name for a collaboration-scale discovery, with AMANDA, DUMAND and Baikal pioneers outside the credit), and the support comes only from Danielsson and the chair.
Every member who addresses B039 treats the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang as a real weakness that cannot be repaired within the supplied names, and none proposes adding a name.
Seven members prefer a single-part prize and one (Danielsson) a two-part prize of three laureates; no configuration exceeds the three-laureate limit.

Members who comment on a possible pairing of topological candidates (Eriksson, Olsson, Pearce) agree that the topological-insulator field should not be split across two prize parts, and Mehlig and Johansson do not propose a second topological part either.
Members who give a conflict note report no recusal ground for the leading candidates B039, B022 and B003.
scientific_disputes: Relative scientific weight of B039 and B022: B039 supporters point to a new classification of electronic phases by band topology with reach into photonics and cold atoms; B022 supporters point to a singular, measurable invention that changes what can be measured and feeds into fundamental tests. Kroll concedes that topological insulators have wider influence across condensed matter.

Whether B039 is a distinct achievement from the 2016 topological-phases prize: Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce argue it extends to time-reversal-invariant materials; Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce also list the overlap as a reservation.

Whether B022 is a distinct achievement from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes: Danielsson, Kroll and Lindroth say yes because of the neutral-atom magic-wavelength concept; Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig describe it as close to or a refinement of that lineage.

Whether the committee can regard the flux evidence for B003 as sufficient for a prize while most of the diffuse flux has no identified source and second-detector confirmation is limited, as noted by Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth and the chair.
Whether B001 (quantum cascade laser) is physics or engineering, raised by Johansson and Olsson, with only two members ranking it in the opening.
attribution_disputes: B039: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (whose HgTe proposal guided Molenkamp's experiment; Zhang died in 2018) and the 3D work of Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan and others lie outside the trio. Several members state that they rely on recollection for this priority history and that it is unverified.

B039 citation boundary: members who address it favour a 2D quantum spin Hall and Z2 citation, but it is not yet shown that this wording keeps the omitted HgTe theorists from looking dismissed, and a broader wording would require 3D names outside the supplied credit.
B003: a single laureate (Halzen) against the AMANDA, DUMAND and Baikal pioneers and the wider IceCube collaboration; no second name is available within the supplied credit.

B022: the two-name credit is the cleanest on the shortlist, but ion-clock groups and other lattice-clock groups (including Lemonde, Gill and Lisdat as named by Kroll and Lindroth) are outside it; Kroll asks that Ye's role be described as precision and many-body control, not only as demonstration.

B025: members choose different three-name subsets of the four credited names (Bloch, Cirac, Greiner, Zoller): Eriksson and the chair choose Cirac, while Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig and Olsson choose Greiner. This suggests that a clean allocation is not yet available, though no member lists B025 in a preferred configuration.
maturity_disputes: B022: whether the still-pending redefinition of the SI second should count as a maturity milestone (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson and Danielsson as a caution) or is irrelevant to physics merit (Kroll, Lindroth and the chair as a timing point, not a flaw).

B039: about two decades of independent confirmation is cited as maturity by its supporters; the open maturity question is overlap with 2016 and limited practical applications, so the case is conceptual and experimental, not technological.

B035 (magic-angle graphene): Eriksson ranks it second and lists it as an alternative, but Mehlig and Johansson say the origin of the correlated states and superconductivity is still debated and the experiments are about eight years old.
B003: the main discovery is secure, but the flux sources are not identified and independent second-detector confirmation is limited, so some members treat it as not yet ready for this year.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: works in superconducting circuits and circuit/waveguide QED, directs WACQT at Chalmers, and has Chalmers colleagues and a frequent co-author; would recuse or flag if B023 or any superconducting-circuit configuration became a serious option. B023 is in no member's configuration.

Kroll: documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder (Hall shared the 2005 prize behind the background to B022); Ye is closely associated with JILA, but no specific tie to Katori or Ye is documented. Kroll also works in quantum memories and WACQT-related technology adjacent to B005 and B023.
Olsson: discloses that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague on the committee, not a candidate; no tie to any credited name.
Eriksson: first-principles electronic structure and magnetism is adjacent to topological band theory; he flags this as possible bias toward condensed-matter candidates, not a recusal ground.
Pearce (chair): ranked B003 first and works in the neighbouring astroparticle field, but no collaboration with IceCube is recorded; no conflict is apparent for B039, B022 or B003.
Danielsson, Lindroth and Mehlig: no specific conflict apparent; Lindroth notes field proximity as an atomic theorist, not a personal connection.
questions_for_round2: For the five B039 supporters: is the committee prepared to adopt a citation scoped to the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 invariant, and how should it be worded so that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction and the 3D work are acknowledged as outside the citation and not disregarded?

For Kroll, Lindroth and Danielsson: does the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang outweigh the B039 theory-to-experiment chain, or would any of you support B039 if the citation were scoped to the 2D case?
For the B039 supporters: what specifically is new relative to the 2016 prize on topological phases, and can that distinction be stated in a sentence that the committee can defend?

For the B022 supporters: does the committee accept a third recognition in the optical-frequency-metrology lineage (2005, 2012), and how would a citation separate the lattice clock from the comb and ion-control prizes and describe Ye's contribution?
Should the pending redefinition of the SI second be treated as a maturity criterion for B022 at all, and would a formal redefinition change any member's ranking between B022 and B039?
For Danielsson and the chair: is there any defensible multi-name credit for B003 within the supplied names, and if not, does either of you still want it in a preferred configuration this year?
Given the three-laureate limit, does any member support a two-part configuration (for example B039 with B022) that exceeds three laureates, and if so, which should be dropped?
Can members who relied on recollection for the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and 3D priority history (Johansson, Olsson, Mehlig, Pearce) say which points they consider settled and which remain open?
summary.chair_observation: In round 1 five of eight members explicitly prefer B039 alone, two prefer B022 alone, and one prefers B022 with B003. Every member who discusses B039 names the missing Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang credit as its main weakness, and the B022 supporters give the clean two-name credit as its main strength, so round 2 should compare these two attribution problems directly. Olsson and Pearce state that their B039 preference changed after reading the opening ballots, so opening support figures should not be read as settled merit. B003 has no preferred-configuration support beyond Danielsson, and the chair has himself moved it to an alternative.
